title: Accelerating Inference for Multilayer Neural Networks with Quantum Computers
claim: One processing architecture is specialized into variants that differ only in how input and weights are provided, each with stated guarantees.
layout: 3 stacked rows (a-c), left-to-right, dashed repeated-block box with skip arrow
description: Three horizontal rows, labeled (a), (b) and (c), show variants of one convolutional network. Each row starts with a colored cat image, a stack of channels, on the left. Row (a) concatenates the channels. Rows (b) and (c) split the input into d copies, each passing through a gray 'Neural Net' box with a head icon, then combining with a tensor-product symbol. After that, each row runs left to right through blue and teal blocks. These are Normalize, a dashed gray box marked ×k that holds stacked 2D Conv layers, Erf, a skip-connection plus sign and Normalize, then Flatten, Square, Linear, Normalize, L2 Pool and Square. The row ends in a bar chart with an arrow marking the top bar and a black 'Cat' label. Row (c) is shorter, with no Square or Linear block. The eye goes first to the cat images and the large conv stacks.
caption: Architecture for Convolutional Neural Networks. This figure shows the architectures we consider with provable quantum complexity guarantees for inference under three regimes of quantum data access assumptions. (a) Depicts the architecture where both the inputs and network weights are provided in an efficient quantum data structure. (b) Only the network weights are provided in an efficient quantum data structure. (c) No input assumptions are made. In all architectures, the input is assumed to be a rank-3 tensor (e.g., images with 4 channels).
abstract: Fault-tolerant Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) promise to deliver exponential speed-ups in select computational tasks, yet their integration into modern deep learning pipelines remains unclear. In this work, we take a step towards bridging this gap by presenting the first fully-coherent quantum implementation of a multilayer neural network with non-linear activation functions. Our constructions mirror widely used deep learning architectures based on ResNet, and consist of residual blocks with multi-filter 2D convolutions, sigmoid activations, skip-connections, and layer normalizations. We analyse the complexity of inference for networks under three quantum data access regimes. Without any assumptions, we establish a quadratic speedup over classical methods for shallow bilinear-style networks. With efficient quantum access to the weights, we obtain a quartic speedup over classical methods. With efficient quantum access to both the inputs and the network weights, we prove that a network with an $N$-dimensional vectorized input, $k$ residual block layers, and a final residual-linear-pooling layer can be implemented with an error of $Îµ$ with $O(\text{polylog}(N/Îµ)^k)$ inference cost.
